questions.q: What is the single most common mistake in a real zero trust maturity assessment, according to this lesson?
options: Scoring what the design aims for instead of what's actually deployed today
Using the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model at all
Asking the budget committee for input before scoring
Scoring every pillar as Traditional by default
questions.explain: Mixing today's real state with the target design's state is the mistake this lesson warns against directly.

questions.q: Why does Meridian's Data pillar stay at Initial even in the target column, right after Lesson 29's design is complete?
options: Because patient data was never classified at all
Because Data enforcement wasn't in scope for any phase
Because the design classified PHI but hasn't yet built enforcement that acts on that classification everywhere it lives
Because the CISA model doesn't include a Data pillar
questions.explain: Classification is step one; enforcing it across every system that holds the data is the harder, separate step that hasn't happened yet.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend reporting five separate pillar scores instead of one blended maturity percentage?
options: A blended score is required by CISA and cannot be changed
Five scores take less time to calculate than one
Pillar scores can only be computed separately for technical reasons
A single blended number hides which pillar is the real risk and can lead a committee to fund the easiest pillar instead of the riskiest one
questions.explain: Averaging pillars together obscures exactly the kind of unevenness -- like Data lagging behind -- that should be driving funding decisions.

questions.q: Why does the roadmap sequence Identity and Networks in Phase 1, ahead of Data enforcement?
options: Data enforcement is sequenced first in every real zero trust rollout
Identity and Networks are mostly configuration against existing licensing, cutting the most risk for the least disruption, while Data enforcement touches every system holding PHI
Identity and Networks have no effect on risk reduction
The CISA model requires pillars to be addressed in alphabetical order
questions.explain: This follows Chapter 7's sequencing principle: risk reduction per unit of effort, not an arbitrary or alphabetical pillar order.

questions.q: In the roadmap one-pager format, what do the whyItMatters and riskIfDelayed fields accomplish?
options: They list the specific CVE numbers associated with each phase
They are optional fields rarely included in a real roadmap
They translate the phase into plain-language risk a non-technical budget committee can act on
They replace the need for any cost estimate
questions.explain: A line like 'one compromised workstation can reach every patient record' is what actually gets budget approved, not Conditional Access terminology.
